# End-to-End Goal-Driven Web Navigation

Introduces WebNav for converting websites into goal-directed hyperlink navigation tasks and WikiNav for evaluating language-conditioned navigation and question answering on Wikipedia.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-1602-02261/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.02261
- Kind: paper

# Mapping Natural Language Commands to Web Elements

Defines language grounding on webpages as choosing the UI element targeted by a natural-language command. A collection of more than 50,000 commands and three baseline models study functional references, relationships between elements, and visual position cues.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-1808-09132/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09132
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web
- Topics: grounding, data-generation, evaluation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-16T06:31:20Z
- ID: arxiv:1808.09132

# Interactive Task and Concept Learning from Natural Language Instructions and GUI Demonstrations

Introduces PUMICE, an agent that learns mobile-app procedures and conditional concepts through natural-language conversation and GUI demonstrations, recursively resolving ambiguous instructions with users.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-1909-00031/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.00031
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: unspecified

# Mapping Natural Language Instructions to Mobile UI Action Sequences

Introduces PIXELHELP for predicting mobile UI action sequences from instructions, together with action-phrase annotations and synthetic UI action descriptions for training. Separate Transformers extract instruction steps and ground object descriptions using interface content and screen position.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2005-03776/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.03776
- Kind: paper

# Object Detection for Graphical User Interface: Old Fashioned or Deep Learning or a Combination?

Compares seven traditional and learned GUI element detectors on more than 50,000 interface images. The analysis motivates a coarse-to-fine non-text detector combined with a learned text detector to address GUI-specific localization requirements.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2008-05132/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.05132
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: unspecified
- Topics: grounding, screen-understanding, evaluation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-16T06:42:42Z

# Widget Captioning: Generating Natural Language Description for Mobile User Interface Elements

Introduces crowdsourced descriptions of mobile UI elements and studies multimodal models that generate useful widget captions.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2010-04295/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.04295
- Kind: paper

# Responsible Task Automation: Empowering Large Language Models as Responsible Task Automators

Presents ResponsibleTA, a coordinator-executor framework that checks command feasibility and task completion while using local memory for privacy-related controls. The paper compares prompted and learned implementations and evaluates them on UI task automation.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2306-01242/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.01242
- Kind: paper

# Synapse: Trajectory-as-Exemplar Prompting with Memory for Computer Control

Synapse filters task-irrelevant page state and places complete abstracted state-action trajectories into the prompt. An embedding-based exemplar memory retrieves relevant demonstrations for new tasks, evaluated on MiniWoB++ and Mind2Web.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2306-07863/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.07863
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated

# WebWISE: Web Interface Control and Sequential Exploration with Large Language Models

WebWISE filters DOM elements into observations and generates short programs for click, scroll, and text-entry steps. It evaluates in-context learning from either one supplied example or an example collected during a successful zero-shot MiniWoB++ trial.

# WILBUR: Adaptive In-Context Learning for Robust and Accurate Web Agents

WILBUR learns to rank prior task demonstrations for a web agent’s prompt and synthesizes instructions from past runs. A generated task curriculum and a backtracking mechanism support adaptation and recovery, evaluated on WebVoyager.

# Tell Me What's Next: Textual Foresight for Generic UI Representations

Textual Foresight learns UI representations by describing the future screen expected after an action on the current interface. The OpenApp dataset supports pretraining and downstream evaluation of representations that connect individual elements with whole-screen changes.

# Seeing is Believing: Vision-driven Non-crash Functional Bug Detection for Mobile Apps

Trident combines exploration, monitoring, and detection agents to identify functional bugs that do not crash a mobile app. It reasons over screenshot sequences and interface transitions to construct test oracles, evaluated on 590 non-crash bugs and additional live apps.

# WebPilot: A Versatile and Autonomous Multi-Agent System for Web Task Execution with Strategic Exploration

WebPilot separates global subtask planning from local Monte Carlo tree search during web execution. It continually refines the high-level plan and adapts local search to uncertain transitions and incomplete observations, evaluated on WebArena and MiniWoB++.

# Synatra: Turning Indirect Knowledge into Direct Demonstrations for Digital Agents at Scale

Synatra converts indirect procedural knowledge, including human-oriented tutorials, into direct demonstrations for digital agents. It trains a 7B CodeLlama on 100,000 synthesized demonstrations and evaluates the resulting policy on Mind2Web, MiniWoB++, and WebArena.

# GUI-Shift: Enhancing VLM-Based GUI Agents through Self-supervised Reinforcement Learning

GUI-Shift trains an inverse-dynamics task that predicts the initial action connecting two GUI states, using trajectories without natural-language instructions. It combines rule-based reinforcement learning with data filtering and evaluates transfer to Android automation and screenshot grounding.

# GEM: Gaussian Embedding Modeling for Out-of-Distribution Detection in GUI Agents

GEM detects instructions outside a GUI agent’s capabilities by modeling distances in its input-embedding space with a Gaussian mixture. Experiments across mobile, computer and browser data also examine selective escalation to a cloud model when an input is detected as unfamiliar.

# GUI-explorer: Autonomous Exploration and Mining of Transition-aware Knowledge for GUI Agent

GUI-explorer generates exploration goals from screenshots and interface structure, then mines observation-action-outcome triples for app-specific transition knowledge. The resulting training-free agent uses this knowledge during mobile task execution, evaluated on SPA-Bench and AndroidWorld.

# ProgRM: Build Better GUI Agents with Progress Rewards

ProgRM predicts per-step task completion progress to provide intermediate rewards during online GUI-agent training. It derives progress labels by using longest common subsequences to identify key trajectory steps, allowing useful partial progress to contribute even when a trajectory ultimately fails.

UI-Genie jointly improves a mobile GUI agent and a reward model that processes screenshots with interaction history and supplies action- and task-level feedback. # GUIPilot: A Consistency-based Mobile GUI Testing Approach for Detecting Application-specific Bugs

Introduces GUIPilot, which compares mobile design mock-ups with implemented screens through widget alignment and tests expected transitions by executing inferred UI actions. It evaluates both visual inconsistencies and workflow-specific bugs.

# MCPWorld: A Unified Benchmarking Testbed for API, GUI, and Hybrid Computer Use Agents

MCPWorld evaluates API, GUI, and hybrid computer-use agents with 201 tasks in applications whose source can be instrumented and extended with MCP support. It verifies completion from application behavior and packages the testbed in containers with GPU support.

# Thinking vs. Doing: Agents that Reason by Scaling Test-Time Interaction

Test-Time Interaction scales the interaction horizon so web agents can explore, backtrack and revise plans within a rollout. Its online reinforcement-learning curriculum adjusts rollout lengths and is evaluated on WebVoyager and WebArena.

# GUI-Reflection: Empowering Multimodal GUI Models with Self-Reflection Behavior

GUI-Reflection synthesizes reflection and error-correction examples from successful trajectories and adds dedicated learning stages for these behaviors. It introduces a reflection task suite, a mobile environment for online data collection, and iterative reflection tuning.

# LPO: Towards Accurate GUI Agent Interaction via Location Preference Optimization

Location Preference Optimization uses an information-entropy signal to select interaction regions and a distance-based reward to assess click locations. It trains GUI localization through preference optimization and evaluates both offline grounding and online interaction.

# MobileGUI-RL: Advancing Mobile GUI Agent through Reinforcement Learning in Online Environment

MobileGUI-RL constructs an online training curriculum through agent exploration and task filtering. It adapts GRPO with trajectory-aware advantages and rewards for task completion and execution efficiency, evaluated on three online mobile-agent benchmarks.

# GTA1: GUI Test-time Scaling Agent

GTA1 samples multiple action proposals at each GUI step and uses a judge to select among them. A separate grounding model is trained with reinforcement learning to map selected proposals to visual targets, linking planning-time search with click localization.

# NaturalGAIA: A Verifiable Benchmark and Hierarchical Framework for Long-Horizon GUI Tasks

NaturalGAIA builds verifiable long-horizon GUI tasks from human interaction intents while separating causal task structure from its verbal description. # SEAgent: Self-Evolving Computer Use Agent with Autonomous Learning from Experience

SEAgent explores unfamiliar software using a world-state assessor and an automatically generated task curriculum. It learns from failed and successful interactions through adversarial imitation and GRPO, then combines specialist experience into a generalist agent evaluated on five OSWorld software environments.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2508-04700/

# UI-S1: Advancing GUI Automation via Semi-online Reinforcement Learning

UI-S1 simulates multi-turn online learning over offline trajectories, using a patch module to recover divergences while retaining the model’s own outputs in context. It combines discounted future returns with step- and episode-level advantages and introduces a semi-online performance proxy.

TGPO merges semantically equivalent web states into tree-structured trajectories for offline preference optimization. A process reward model scores subgoal progress, redundant behavior, and action validity, while dynamic weighting emphasizes consequential decisions.

GUI-ARP uses visual attention to crop relevant screenshot regions and decides whether a target needs single-stage or multi-stage analysis. Supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO trains this adaptive procedure for high-resolution GUI grounding.

BTL-UI separates GUI interaction into screen-region attention, planning and executable-command generation. It adds an automated annotation pipeline and rule-based process/outcome rewards for training, with evaluation on both static understanding and dynamic interaction.

# UIPro: Unleashing Superior Interaction Capability For GUI Agents

UIPro pretrains GUI understanding on 20.6 million tasks and then harmonizes interaction datasets through a unified action space. Continued fine-tuning uses the merged multi-platform data to train action prediction for generalist GUI operation.

# CORE: Reducing UI Exposure in Mobile Agents via Collaboration Between Cloud and Local LLMs

Introduces CORE, which divides mobile UI hierarchies into semantic blocks and shares planning between local and cloud language models. Local ranking limits the screen information sent for cloud-side element selection, with a multi-round mechanism for correcting inadequate context.

# HiconAgent: History Context-aware Policy Optimization for GUI Agents

HiconAgent trains GUI policies to use history through variable-length context sampling and paired policy updates with compressed and complete histories. Its compression retains past actions while removing historical observations, and an alignment loss couples the two branches.

# OS-Oracle: A Comprehensive Framework for Cross-Platform GUI Critic Models

OS-Oracle synthesizes GUI critic examples and trains a pre-action critic with supervised learning followed by consistency-preserving GRPO. It introduces OS-Critic Bench across mobile, web, and desktop settings and tests critic-assisted agents in OSWorld and AndroidWorld.

# EchoTrail-GUI: Building Actionable Memory for GUI Agents via Critic-Guided Self-Exploration

EchoTrail-GUI builds a memory of successful GUI trajectories through autonomous exploration filtered by a reward model. It retrieves relevant trajectories as in-context guidance for new tasks and evaluates the approach on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.

# ProSoftArena: Benchmarking Hierarchical Capabilities of Multimodal Agents in Professional Software Environments

ProSoftArena evaluates 436 professional-software tasks across six disciplines and 13 applications in a Windows 11 virtual-machine environment. Its capability hierarchy, execution-based checks, and human-in-the-loop evaluation cover precise GUI operations and multi-software workflows.

# FocusUI: Efficient UI Grounding via Position-Preserving Visual Token Selection

# Curiosity Driven Knowledge Retrieval for Mobile Agents

Uses execution uncertainty to trigger retrieval from application documentation, code, and past trajectories, organizing the results into structured AppCards for Android agent planning.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2601-19306/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19306
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: android
- Topics: memory, planning, mobile-navigation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-18T10:01:04.629294+00:00
- ID: arxiv:2601.19306

## Limitations

The curiosity signal is a model-based proxy, not a calibrated probability of failure. Accurate external app information is a dependency, and AndroidWorld is the reported evaluation environment. No performance numbers were independently reproduced. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (3.1 Problem Formulation; 3.2 Curiosity-Driven Information Gain Estimation; 3.3 Retrieving and Embedding External Knowledge); not an entire-paper reading or reproduction claim.

CovAgent augments Android GUI fuzzers by analyzing decompiled app code and component transitions to identify unsatisfied activation conditions. A second agent generates instrumentation that enables otherwise difficult-to-reach activities, with coverage-based evaluation.

# SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration

Introduces SafeGround, which estimates GUI-grounding uncertainty from the spatial dispersion of sampled predictions and calibrates a decision threshold before testing. It studies risk-aware selection on ScreenSpot-Pro, with statistical control scoped to the threshold’s false-discovery rate.

# A11y-CUA Dataset: Characterizing the Accessibility Gap in Computer Use Agents

Introduces A11y-CUA, a dataset comparing how blind or low-vision users and sighted users perform everyday computer tasks. It contrasts those traces with agent behavior under default, keyboard-only, and magnifier conditions to identify barriers to shared control.

# OpAgent: Operator Agent for Web Navigation

OpAgent combines multi-task GUI fine-tuning with online web reinforcement learning using outcome judgments and rule-based progress rewards. A modular planner, grounder, reflector and summarizer support navigation and recovery, evaluated separately from the underlying trained policy.

# Building Autonomous GUI Navigation via Agentic-Q Estimation and Step-Wise Policy Optimization

This framework learns an agentic-Q model to estimate individual actions’ contributions to GUI task completion. It then optimizes a policy with step-level samples from its own trajectories, decoupling policy updates from environment interaction.

# MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks

MemoryArena links tasks across sessions so that agents must distill earlier interaction experience and use it in later decisions. Its evaluation includes web navigation alongside planning, search and formal reasoning, testing memory through subsequent actions rather than recall alone.

# AgentRAE: Remote Action Execution through Notification-based Visual Backdoors against Screenshots-based Mobile GUI Agents

AgentRAE studies notification-based visual backdoors that redirect mobile GUI-agent actions. Its training separates sensitivity to icon differences from trigger/action association, with evaluations of clean behavior and targeted redirection.

# CarePilot: A Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Computer Task Automation in Healthcare

CareFlow benchmarks long healthcare-software workflows, while CarePilot coordinates action proposals, execution checks and corrective feedback using short- and long-term memory. Its actor consumes visual interfaces and system state to select semantic actions.

# CUA-Suite: Massive Human-annotated Video Demonstrations for Computer-Use Agents

CUA-Suite combines continuous expert desktop demonstrations in VideoCUA with the UI-Vision evaluation benchmark and GroundCUA grounding data. Screen recordings, cursor traces and layered annotations support study of temporal behavior and professional software workflows.

# UI-Voyager: A Self-Evolving GUI Agent Learning via Failed Experience

Introduces a two-stage mobile GUI learner that first co-evolves trajectories and policies through rejection fine-tuning. Group Relative Self-Distillation then uses successful rollout branches to provide step-level supervision for failed trajectories, evaluated on AndroidWorld.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2603-24533/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24533

# GUIDE: A Benchmark for Understanding and Assisting Users in Open-Ended GUI Tasks

GUIDE evaluates whether models can recognize a user’s behavior, infer intent and decide when to offer help during open-ended software tasks. It uses narrated screen recordings of novice users and studies the effect of additional user context on these assistance decisions.

# Are GUI Agents Focused Enough? Automated Distraction via Semantic-level UI Element Injection

This study tests black-box GUI-grounding failures caused by strategically added, innocuous-looking UI elements. Its iterative overlay search is compared with random injection and repeated independent grounding trials to distinguish persistent misdirection from incidental clutter.

# CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation

Introduces CORA, which calibrates a risk model to choose between executing and abstaining from mobile GUI actions, then diagnoses rejected actions to suggest interventions. Phone-Harm provides step-level safety labels for evaluating this safeguarding process.

# TClone: Low-Latency Forking of Live GUI Environments for Computer-Use Agents

TClone versions live GUI workspaces through snapshots, isolated forks, rollback and selective commit or merge. It separates fast branch creation from durable checkpoints using copy-on-write sharing, filesystem versioning and asynchronous checkpointing, with end-to-end agent-loop latency measurements.

MementoGUI learns a controller for selecting, compressing and retrieving textual and region-level visual memories while leaving the GUI-agent backbone fixed. MobileExplorer probes relevant UI elements while an on-device model is reasoning, then supplies the exploration trace as compact context. A two-level rollback mechanism restores the working state when simple backtracking fails.

# AsyncWebRL: Efficient Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Step Visual Web Agents

AsyncWebRL overlaps web-agent rollouts, updates and policy refresh while managing screenshot handling and a persistent rollout pool. It also replaces trajectory-length normalization in multi-step GRPO to reduce verbose failed trajectories, with throughput and out-of-distribution evaluation.

# Signal-Driven Observation for Long-Horizon Web Agents

Proposes Signal-Driven Observation: a separate call selects relevant DOM elements and selectors, and a detector requests new observations only after meaningful browser events or failures. The paper frames observation timing and compression as an architectural research problem for long-horizon web agents.

# PreAct: Computer-Using Agents that Get Faster on Repeated Tasks

PreAct compiles successful screen-interaction runs into guarded state-machine programs for repeated tasks. It validates programs from clean states before storage and returns control to the agent when replayed screen expectations fail, with tests across mobile, desktop and web.

# Skill-Guided Continuation Distillation for GUI Agents

# MemGUI-Agent: An End-to-End Long-Horizon Mobile GUI Agent with Proactive Context Management

MemGUI-Agent makes context management an action chosen by the same policy that controls the mobile UI. Structured history, UI-state and recent-step fields are trained from annotated trajectories to retain cross-app facts while limiting context growth.

# ENVS: Environment-Native Verified Search for Long-Horizon GUI Agents

ENVS branches over GUI actions in live desktop VMs, verifies successful leaves, and converts them into balanced step-level training supervision. It also introduces OSWorld-Noisy to test recovery from dynamic interruptions while retaining the underlying tasks.

# Uncertainty Quantification for Computer-Use Agents: A Benchmark across Vision-Language Models and GUI Grounding Datasets

Argus benchmarks post-hoc uncertainty methods for single-step GUI grounding across open-weight and closed-source observation regimes. # WinDOM: Self-Family Distillation for Small-Model GUI Grounding

WinDOM obtains bounding-box supervision from a Windows 11 web reimplementation driven through Playwright, and studies rejection-sampling distillation for small GUI grounders. It treats the depth of the supervised cold start as a GRPO choice, comparing same-size EMA and larger same-family teachers.

# One Forward Beats Two: InnerZoom for Accurate and Efficient GUI Grounding

InnerZoom preserves target-region cues from intermediate decoder layers and reinjects a compact evidence state during coordinate decoding. Its single-forward GUI grounder is compared with crop-and-rerun zooming and matched supervised/RL baselines for accuracy and inference cost.

Evaluates web agents against anti-bot mechanisms on instrumented honeysites and analyzes network, HTTP and browser fingerprints. The study compares resistance to blocking with the ability to distinguish agents, humans and agent implementations.

# LUMOS: A Semantic Operating-System Layer for Accessibility-Grounded AI Agents

LUMOS converts native accessibility metadata and browser UI structure into semantic interface blueprints with stable element identifiers and available actions. It combines live pointer-to-element grounding with an observe-act loop constrained to visible-UI primitives.

# DigitalCoach: Communication and Grounding Gaps in Human and Agentic Computer Use Coaching

DigitalCoach records expert–novice software coaching conversations aligned with screen and input events. Automated and interactive evaluations examine how model coaches differ from humans in explanation, error diagnosis and visual grounding when helping a learner operate software.

# UI-MOPD: Multi-Platform On-Policy Distillation for Unified GUI Agents

Introduces Uni-GUI, a collection of executable desktop and mobile trajectories, and UI-MOPD, which trains a shared policy from its own rollouts using platform-specific teachers. The distillation procedure routes each visited state to the appropriate teacher to preserve distinct interaction conventions.

# Untrusted Content Masking for Web Agents with Security Guarantees

Untrusted Content Masking uses DOM structure to redact untrusted webpage regions before agent observation. A sandboxed interaction interface separates privileges so browser actions can proceed under the proposed trust-boundary model without exposing protected content to the planner.

# StateAct: Program State, before Pixels, for Long-Horizon Computer-Use Agents

Introduces StateAct, a code-first computer-use harness that manipulates program state directly and delegates screenshot-and-click subgoals to a GUI agent. An independent completion gate checks saved outputs, while fresh subagents handle subgoals to limit accumulated context.

# MAGA: Multi-Platform Self-Fusion of GUI Agents via Structured Action Distillation

MAGA distills specialized GUI agents into one policy by allocating supervision according to structured-action correctness rather than treating all response tokens equally. A training-only teacher hint supports fusion across mobile, web and desktop settings without changing student inputs.

# LookAgain: Closed-Loop GUI Grounding with Visually Grounded Reflection

# LegacyWorld: Atomicity-Aware Evaluation of GUI Agents for Legacy Workflows

LegacyWorld evaluates Windows GUI workflows under an atomicity criterion: finish correctly or fail without persistent unintended changes. It compares expert prompts with prompts derived from recorded golden paths and separates useful completion, safe failure and non-atomic side effects.

# CURA: Certified Runtime Alarms for Computer-Use Agents

# Iron: Intent-Aligned and Retrospective Dual Learning Framework for Enhancing Generalist Virtual Agents

# SIR: Self-improving Red-teaming for Compute Use Agents

Introduces SIR, which iteratively refines a reusable library of prompt-injection strategies from failed computer-use attack trajectories. Its evaluation uses deterministic system-state checks and counts attacks only when the adversarial objective and legitimate task both complete.

# GUI-CC: Benchmarking Contextual Consistency of GUI World Models as Agent Environments

Introduces GUI-CC, a benchmark for assessing GUI world models as multi-step agent environments. Separate reference-action and agent-loop tracks test whether generated screens preserve context, plausible transitions, and task progress throughout interaction.

# Monitoring Web Agents Without Internal Signals: Observable Trajectories and Key-Step Supervision

Predicts web-agent failure risk from observable trajectory prefixes using cross-step behavior and black-box consistency queries. Key-step labels preserve valid early prefixes of failed runs, and evaluation tests early intervention and transfer across website categories.

# From Interaction Traces to Persistent Skills: Online Evolution for Computer-Use Agents

An online skill-evolution framework turns GUI interaction traces and evaluator feedback into a versioned library of reusable procedures without updating model parameters. # SCAFFOLD: Self-Improving Web Agents via Recursive Parametric Skill Abstraction

Introduces SCAFFOLD, which extracts executable skills from web trajectories, composes them into a hierarchy, and compresses redundant skills through behavioral checks. It periodically distills skill-guided trajectories into the policy and studies repeated improvement across web benchmarks.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2609-05511/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05511
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web

Introduces CAVEAT, a controlled marketplace benchmark for testing whether delegated agents preserve user objectives when interfaces favor other outcomes. It diagnoses decision failures and studies harness interventions and targeted training to improve resistance to marketplace steering.

# Learn How to Act from Your Own Interactions: On-Policy Self-Distillation for GUI Agents

GUI-SD-v2 extends on-policy self-distillation from grounding to multi-turn GUI interaction. It first strengthens responses to privileged guidance, then selectively distills step-specific reasoning and memory support for later actions.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2609-27307/

# Guides That Cause Actions: An Offline Study of Guide-Action Mutual Reinforcement in Multimodal Web Agents

WebMRE pairs guidance sentences with grounded actions in an offline benchmark derived from successful WebArena traces. Controlled decoding-prefix interventions test how guide content affects action selection, while separating offline prediction metrics from live browser task success.

# Invisible in Space, Visible in Time: Motion Vision CAPTCHA against GUI Agents

MVCAP-Bench tests live browser CAPTCHAs whose foreground meaning emerges through motion against dynamic backgrounds. A foreground-only control separates temporal camouflage difficulty from answer format and browser interaction.

# Improving LLM-based Autonomous Web Agents with Filtering

Trains HTML-element relevance filters on Mind2Web trajectories and transfers them to WebArena to reduce irrelevant browser context. It also evaluates a zero-shot ColBERT retriever and documents baseline web-agent failure modes.

# Qwen-Planner-Agent: A Closed-Loop AI-for-AI Framework for Real-World Mobile Planner Agents

Trains a mobile planner with supervised trajectories and competence-adaptive RL, then couples typed tool execution with memory, skills and offline model-harness refinement.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2609-29892/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29892
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: unspecified
- Topics: planning, data-generation, reinforcement-learning, memory, mobile-navigation, efficiency
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T15:43:20.402537Z
- ID: arxiv:2609.29892

## Limitations

Primarily typed tool actions and structured feedback, not pixel-coordinate GUI control; backends combine programmatic sandboxes, LLM simulation and selected real-device sessions. No specific OS is established. Model/harness updates are reviewed offline, not autonomous serving-time changes. Co-evolution scores use an evolve/development set; output-cost estimates exclude input, tools, devices and harness processing. Memory comparisons differ in history access and processing cost; user authorization relies on trusted upstream services. No independent reproduction.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2609-29892/record.json

# OpenVAM: Open-World Visual Attention Modeling with VLMs

Combines dense saliency prediction with explanations of attended elements, including webpage layouts; evaluates human-attention agreement and textual rationales rather than agent actions.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2609-31364/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31364
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: adjacent
- Environments: web
- Topics: screen-understanding, ui-design, evaluation, data-generation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T19:01:29.156954Z
- ID: arxiv:2609.31364

## Limitations

Static human-attention modeling on U-EYE webpage screenshots, with FIWI held out from training; no live-browser, agent-action or task-success evaluation. Gemini-generated reference rationales are expert-checked, and JScore compares generated text with references; human validation covers a separate 100-image subset. Reference text and heatmap alignment do not establish causal explanations of gaze or temporal scanpaths. Several baseline scores come from prior papers. Code/data/weight releases and licenses were not verified; no independent reproduction.

# Learning from Others, Acting for You: Cross-User Memory Sharing for LLM Agents

ShareMem consolidates reusable experience across users while keeping preference retrieval user-bound; its web evaluation predicts target elements and actions on recorded Mind2Web states.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2609-32511/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32511
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web
- Topics: memory, web-navigation, action-prediction, evaluation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T15:08:56Z
- ID: arxiv:2609.32511

## Limitations

Main Mind2Web evaluation uses 252 recorded tasks assigned to 20 simulated users, frozen demonstration-derived memory and task-macro step metrics; it is not a live-browser completion test. The main split withholds same-site local experience, and sharing gains shrink when local coverage rises. Mind2Web has no preference channel; preference claims come from separate service and coding settings. User-bound retrieval is not a demonstrated privacy or security guarantee. Selected sections were source-read; no independent reproduction.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2609-32511/record.json

# ORBIT: A Framework for Multi-Agent Safety and Security Evaluations

Inspect-based framework that varies multi-agent roles, communication, attacks and defenses, with BrowserGym and virtual-desktop GUI adapters alongside coding and other tool scenarios.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2609-33102/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33102
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web, desktop
- Topics: evaluation, safety-security, web-navigation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T13:12:28.833839+00:00
- ID: arxiv:2609.33102

## Limitations

BrowserART uses an accessibility-tree action interface, while the desktop adapter uses mouse, keyboard and screenshots. The adapted tasks are not claimed to preserve the constructs of their source benchmarks. Experiments cover a representative configuration slice with fixed attack templates; the OS-Harm results are imported from prior work using a different model and stack. Browser defense tables also differ in baseline versus defended judges and in judged benign denominators. Human judge validation used one grader. These results do not establish a universally effective defense. The linked repository and its code/data licenses were not independently inspected, and no experiment was run.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2609-33102/record.json

## Authors

Ben Hagag, William L. Anderson, Srija Chakraborty, Christian Schroeder de Witt

# One Rollout Is All You Get: Fully Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Agents

Defines a test-time adaptation setting with one counted attempt per arriving GUI task and no ground-truth feedback. Its SOLO method filters or relabels completed episodes, then updates a small adapter from a short window of the agent’s own experience.

# LongPuzzleBench: Evaluating GUI Agents on Long-Horizon Visual Puzzles

LongPuzzleBench evaluates coherent long-horizon planning on persistent visual puzzle boards through native GUI actions. It compares GUI-only and code-assisted agents and uses controlled hints and memory diagnostics to examine decisions that preserve or eliminate future solutions.

Introduces PhoneCLI, which explores mobile app interfaces and compiles navigation paths into reusable commands without internal app APIs or instrumentation. At execution time it verifies compiled paths and falls back to a visual agent for open-ended interaction or failed navigation.

# Constructing Challenging Browser-Use Tasks by Controlled Environment Interventions

BreakingWeb pairs solvable browser tasks with controlled environment interventions that preserve the goal, target and backend success criterion. The paired evaluations isolate robustness failures, including agents declaring completion without the required state change.

# SCOUT: Synergizing Reasoning and Tool-Use for Computer-Use Safety

Introduces SCOUT, a safety verifier that first derives task-specific completion and safety rubrics from a computer-use trajectory, then actively probes the resulting environment for evidence. It evaluates whether these two stages detect harmful consequences that screenshots alone can miss.

# AdaptArena: Evaluating Test-Time Personalization of Web Agents

Introduces AdaptArena to test whether web agents can infer unstated user preferences from relevant past trajectories and carry those preferences into new tasks. Its AdaptiveAgent baseline separates preference-retrieval challenges from failures in downstream web execution.

# Auditing Web Agent Evaluation on WebArena-Lite: Human Review of Outcomes and Trajectories

Audits WebArena-Lite outcomes and trajectories with human review to identify automatic-evaluator false negatives and the first consequential execution errors. It also studies explicit execution-state memory and procedural guidance, showing why final task scores can miss substantial differences in agent behavior.

# How To Train Your World Model: Fine-tuning vs RAG for LM-based World Modeling

Compares fine-tuned, retrieval-based and hybrid language-model world models for next-observation prediction and action selection in text environments including WebShop.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2610-02542/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02542
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: adjacent
- Environments: web
- Topics: world-models, planning, evaluation, web-navigation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T15:08:56Z
- ID: arxiv:2610.02542

## Limitations

Adjacent cross-domain study with WebShop as its web evaluation. WebShop uses text-rendered search/product pages and an explicit valid-action menu, not screenshot control or live purchases. A frozen policy proposes five actions; a world model predicts their next observations and the policy scores them before one is executed in the simulator. Utility is normalized environment reward, while fidelity uses a model judge; neither is a universal GUI task-success rate. Fine-tuning and retrieval use collected training experience; the hybrid masks same-episode retrieval, which does not establish general contamination freedom. The retained Atom and v1 HTML abstract wording differs; original bibliographic metadata and its abstract digest are preserved.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2610-02542/record.json

# AMBER: Training Long-Horizon Web Agents through Append-Only Memory

Introduces AMBER, an append-only memory framework in which a web agent learns to reason, act, and retain evidence using outcome-reward reinforcement learning. It studies whether preserving entries avoids the loss of facts and corrective feedback seen with rewritten memory.

# AgentTime: Can Agents Estimate and Control Their Own Runtime?

Evaluates duration following, runtime forecasts and elapsed-time estimates in native agent harnesses, including OSWorld desktop tasks, with external timers, native graders and work-versus-wait analysis.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2610-09944/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09944
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: desktop
- Topics: evaluation, observability
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T15:08:56.488063+00:00
- ID: arxiv:2610.09944

## Limitations

This cross-domain suite includes 16 OSWorld 2.0 tasks among 222 tasks from 18 sources. A single run per task and requested duration, provider effects and incomplete native grades limit comparisons; elapsed time is not evidence of productive work. The OSWorld task 092 video judge was skipped without an API key. The inspected repository README identifies desktop-VM timing and states that the current 222-task forecasting runs will be added; its existing forecasting code covers an earlier study, and transcript work/wait labels are not public. No code or benchmark was executed and no license was verified.

# DeltaReplay: Task-Relative Memory Reuse for Mobile GUI Agents

Introduces DeltaReplay, which stores mobile GUI trajectories as transition graphs and decides at each step whether to reuse an action, substitute task-specific parameters, or defer to the base agent. This supports reuse of partially matching experiences without rewriting stored memory.

# Right Screen, Wrong Transition: World Models as Verifiers for GUI Agents

# Can LLMs Fix It Without Code? Toward Automated Verification of No-Code Bug Fixes

Tests natural-language no-code fixes through GUI execution in Linux Brave. Scripted fixed/buggy-state gates and issue-specific checkers distinguish fix outcomes from the executor's completion claims.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2610-11963/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11963
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web, desktop, linux
- Topics: evaluation, web-navigation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T13:12:25.581656+00:00
- ID: arxiv:2610.11963

## Limitations

The evaluation reuses 322 fixes from 12 generation configurations and is restricted to nine of 51 candidate issues after environment setup and sanity checks. Resolution counts any success in three runs with a 20-step episode limit; executor harnesses and decoding settings differ. Opening the update page triggers a harness-controlled switch to the fixed browser build. Checker behavior, reconstructed starting states and the two-author human reference limit interpretation. The replication package was linked by the paper but was not inspected; no software, agent, model or result was run or reproduced.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2610-11963/record.json

## Limitations

The mobile evaluation uses text UI observations and one fixed instance for each of 116 AndroidWorld task types; three repeats share seed 0. Five agent families use different budgets, with candidate-interface and tool-call granularity changes in some variants. Reported costs use fixed experimental prices, and outcome-selected trace labels are not population failure rates. Faster selection does not imply faster or more reliable task completion. Selected sections were source-read; no independent reproduction.

# From Observations to Authorized Actions: Measuring Source Information in Android Agents

Measures source-attribution limits in Android accessibility and separately tests application-history and selected-WebView-object checks for authorizing AppFunctions actions.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2610-15502/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15502
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: android, web
- Topics: safety-security, tool-integration, observability
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T13:12:58.069698Z
- ID: arxiv:2610.15502

## Limitations

The two prototypes use different workloads and trust assumptions on patched Android/WebView components. Approval is simulated; authenticated browser delivery and atomic capture remain unimplemented. Coarse source history can withhold benign work and persist across tasks. Direct-call checks and limited live-agent trials are separate, and writes are in-memory. No production vulnerability, general defense rate or released artifact is established.

# Visible but Not Avoided: State-Dependent Re-Proposal of Rejected Candidates in Catalog-Based LLM Optimization Loops

Studies repeated rejected edits while optimizing a screenshot-only GUI agent, contrasting static probes with reached loop states and testing how rejection wording changes subsequent edit proposals.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2610-15738/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15738
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: unspecified
- Topics: evaluation, grounding, training-free
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T15:31:34.620763Z
- ID: arxiv:2610.15738

## Limitations

The downstream test uses one screenshot-only agent, nine synthetic apps and 60 cached development items, with TAP-tag or text-answer outputs; this is not demonstrated live-app completion. Two catalogs reword the same 40 edits. Re-proposal effects do not establish internal causal mechanisms or task-success gains. Main serving providers were unpinned; rationale labels came from LLM annotators. No independent reproduction.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2610-15738/record.json

# Reading Right, Acting Wrong: Diagnosing Decision Failures of System One Models in Agent Loops

Pairs factual probes with next-action choices on frozen agent traces, including Mind2Web, to diagnose reading-decision gaps without closed-loop execution.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2610-18579/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18579
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: adjacent
- Environments: web
- Topics: evaluation, web-navigation, interaction-history
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T15:08:55Z
- ID: arxiv:2610.18579

## Limitations

Adjacent diagnostic research across simulators, policies, tools, coding and an offline Mind2Web subset. Models choose among supplied admissible actions; they do not generate actions or execute a closed-loop browser policy in the reported evaluation. The paired probes measure selected visible facts, not complete understanding or internal causation. Pooled results are not a web-only leaderboard, and the paper reports coverage limits and label-sensitivity analyses. No benchmark release, code, data or weights were independently inspected.

## Limitations

A broad literature synthesis spanning images, video, audio, GUI and embodied settings. # MMA-SafetyBench: A Benchmark for Multimodal Agent Safety Evaluation

Builds trajectory-guided visual-injection tests for web, desktop and mobile observations, separating target-matching action predictions from broader semantic compromise.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2610-19384/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19384
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web, desktop
- Topics: evaluation, safety-security, grounding
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T19:02:16.329923+00:00
- ID: arxiv:2610.19384

## Limitations

ASR measures predicted coordinates inside an annotated target or compromised generated content; actual clicks, environment changes and downstream harm are not verified. SCR additionally counts adopted adversarial intent or task/schema disruption. Clean-task and attacked-trajectory denominators differ, including 42 clean desktop tasks versus 209 adversarial desktop trajectories. Payloads and injection points are fixed, and neutral prompts change both compliance cues and instruction-priority guidance. GPT-5 judging has a 300-trajectory human-label check, with borderline disagreements. Android-style mobile dialogs do not establish an Android runtime. Code/data links were identified but not inspected; no independent reproduction.

# ECHOES: Seeing Beyond the Current Image via Recursive History Compression and Privileged On-Policy Distillation

ECHOES learns recursive textual task memory through privileged screenshot-history distillation and GRPO, then predicts GUI actions from the current screenshot and memory.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2610-22408/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22408
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: android
- Topics: memory, interaction-history, state-tracking, long-horizon, imitation-learning, reinforcement-learning, efficiency, evaluation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T13:12:54.814500Z
- ID: arxiv:2610.22408

## Limitations

Privileged screenshot history is used during training, while deployment retains self-generated textual state. GUI results use action/step metrics and model-specific history settings; online Sokoban transfer is separate. GRPO rewards action correctness, valid output format and compression length. Diagnostic memory replay is distinct from the validation gap used to schedule training. No independent reproduction.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2610-22408/record.json

# Not All Graphs Are Maps: A Task-Agnostic Exploration Framework for Mobile GUI Navigation

TAG-Nav supplies Android GUI agents with destination and route memory distilled from offline app exploration. DestBench measures arrival at a reference pre-action screen, separately from downstream task execution.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2610-22672/
- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22672
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: android
- Topics: mobile-navigation, memory, evaluation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T12:56:56.464343+00:00
- ID: arxiv:2610.22672

## Limitations

The controlled cohort has 84 tasks across six apps; the broader inventory spans 20 apps. Main results use human destination labels. DroidTask and SPA-Bench are converted to navigation-only protocols. Some comparison cells received another graph condition’s memory, with sensitivity analyses reported. Cross-family runs differ in app versions, state and denominators. A small stale-graph probe does not establish robustness. Models, code, artifacts and performance were not independently reproduced.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/arxiv-2610-22672/record.json

- Original source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22697
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web
- Topics: safety-security, web-navigation, planning, human-in-the-loop
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T13:38:46.444001Z
- ID: arxiv:2610.22697

## Limitations

Evaluation instructs the model to simulate compromise and measures planner outputs and permission appearance. Utility uses plan matching and LLM-judged element suitability; no steps are executed in that assessment. Assumes an honest first party, trusted browser/harness and untampered instrumentation; multi-page and availability attacks are outside scope. Parallel latency reduction is an unimplemented estimate. No independent reproduction.

# ScopeMem: Latent Memory That Learns Where to Revise Frozen GUI Agents

ScopeMem conditions latent-memory prefixes on a frozen GUI agent's initial action and trains them to correct errors while preserving correct decisions. Its evaluation separates action repairs from harmful revisions.

# AndroidArena

- Environments: android
- Topics: evaluation, mobile-navigation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-16T06:35:58Z
- ID: github:androidarenaagent/androidarena

## Limitations

Inclusion does not establish reproducibility or endorsement.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-androidarenaagent-androidarena/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: app launch/stop, click/double-click/long-click, text input, swipe/drag and Android navigation, finish
- evaluation: The released evaluator compares trajectories with reference actions using longest-common-subsequence-based task reward and completion. Its reversed redundancy metric is the reference/predicted action-length ratio (with 1e-6 denominator smoothing), multiplied by the LLM success flag. LLM success judgments and instruction-constraint checks are separate metrics. Full reference-dependent evaluation coverage cannot be assumed because complete annotated action sequences are not released.
- focus: multi-step Android tasks, cross-app workflows and instruction constraints
- observations: UI hierarchy text, screenshots, combined text/image observations
- setting: interactive

### Count observations

No count recorded.

README states that task instructions are released but annotated action sequences, apart from the calendar example, will come later. Environment setup targets Android API 33 with uiautomator2 and manual Google-account setup. Public task YAML and evaluator code exist, but benchmark execution and full reference coverage were not verified. No task total is derived from app YAML file counts. Code and data licenses remain unknown.

Windows tray utility that records primary-display screenshots, keyboard key codes and mouse events as local JPEG and JSON files for training-data collection.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-anikasomaia-local-activity-recorder/
- Original source: https://github.com/anikasomaia/local-activity-recorder

- Scope: core
- Environments: desktop, windows
- Topics: recording, data-generation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T11:57:15.716415+00:00
- ID: github:anikasomaia/local-activity-recorder

## Limitations

Recording is started and stopped from the tray; screenshots use a five-second timer. The manual Upload Data action uses a built-in third-party demonstration endpoint unless changed in code, sending recorded files as base64 JSON. Successful uploads move files into uploaded subfolders rather than delete them; no automatic expiry policy was found in the inspected capture/upload path. Sensitive-application filters are listed as future work. The README's .NET version requirements are inconsistent, and long-session behavior was not established. No license declaration was found in the inspected files or complete tree's license-file names, so code permission remains unknown. No activity was captured and no uploader or executable was run.

# GUIHalluBench

Measures hallucination in UI-element parsing by matching the boxes and descriptions a model lists for 1,000 English and 1,000 Chinese screenshots against human annotations.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-ant-research-guihallubench/
- Original source: https://github.com/ant-research/GUIHalluBench
- Kind: benchmark
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: cross-platform
- Topics: evaluation, robustness
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-16T06:40:51Z
- ID: github:ant-research/guihallubench

## Limitations

Inclusion does not establish reproducibility or endorsement.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-ant-research-guihallubench/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: list of UI element boxes [x1,y1,x2,y2] and text descriptions
- evaluation: Metrics use greedy one-to-one matching in descending IoU order, then micro precision/recall/F1 and lowercased difflib.SequenceMatcher description similarity on matched pairs. Actual metrics.py accepts IoU >= 0.5 at its default threshold; README prose says > 0.5. Predictions align to annotations by image_path; callers must supply complete prediction coverage because missing predictions are not independently enumerated by evaluate_dataset.
- focus: GUI page-element detection, element-description consistency
- observations: page screenshot
- setting: offline

### Count observations

- 1,000 page-annotation entries — English annotation subset reported by README (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ant-research/GUIHalluBench/HEAD/README.md)
- 1,000 page-annotation entries — Chinese annotation subset reported by README (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ant-research/GUIHalluBench/HEAD/README.md)

Each annotation entry represents a page, not one UI element. README’s illustrative num_samples=4796 output is not adopted as a corpus count. Public tree contains both annotation JSON files and an images.tar.gz Git-LFS pointer; payload availability/integrity was not tested by downloading images. LEGAL.md only governs comment-language precedence, not a code/data license grant; both slots remain unknown. No benchmark run was performed.

## License declarations

- code: not recorded
- data: not recorded
- document: not recorded
- weights: not recorded

The canonical repository is ByteDance-Seed/Agent-R and is archived but readable. MCTS collection, revision and evaluation scripts are released under Apache-2.0. It also supports non-GUI text environments; this entry covers its WebShop interaction component. No separate weight release was verified.

# GUI-ReWalk

A desktop trajectory-generation framework that moves from stochastic GUI exploration to inferred goals and multi-stage task completion, with retrospective reasoning annotations.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-bytedance-gui-rewalk/
- Original source: https://github.com/bytedance/GUI-ReWalk
- Kind: framework
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: desktop, linux
- Topics: data-generation, planning, cross-app
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-17T09:12:15Z
- ID: github:bytedance/gui-rewalk

## Limitations

The inspected source tree contains the random walker, desktop environment integration and run_rewalk.sh. The documented runnable setup uses OSWorld and OmniParser. The README also discusses mobile data and a GUI-ReWalk-7B model, but no separately published corpus or model checkpoint was verified; those are not counted as released assets. Apache-2.0 is scoped to the implementation.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-bytedance-gui-rewalk/record.json

# Web Context Bench (Python)

Local-page benchmark comparing six browser representations on token use, factual reading and target-element selection, with deterministic answer scoring.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-charlypoly-web-context-bench-python/
- Original source: https://github.com/charlypoly/web-context-bench-python
- Kind: benchmark
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web
- Topics: evaluation, grounding, efficiency, screen-understanding
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T11:51:30.874397Z
- ID: github:charlypoly/web-context-bench-python

## Limitations

This is a single-snapshot representation evaluation on local fixtures and captured pages, not a live multi-step agent benchmark. Its shared-prompt, one-model setup differs from complete Browser Use or Stagehand agents. The methodology notes unresolved redistribution licensing for third-party practice-site snapshots; MIT is recorded for repository code only. Selected scoring code was read, but no models, browser tasks or claimed results were run or reproduced.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-charlypoly-web-context-bench-python/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: READ text answer, ACT selector, text/label, accessible role/name, DOM index, Stagehand reference or screenshot point, according to the representation
- evaluation: READ uses normalized exact match against an answer or allowed alias. ACT resolves predicted identifiers to ground-truth elements, or checks screenshot points inside the target box. Representation-token accounting subtracts fixed-prompt tokens; screenshots use billed input usage minus the fixed prompt. These are answer/target correctness and token metrics, not completed-task success.
- focus: Browser-representation token use, Factual READ accuracy, ACT target-element selection
- observations: Top-document HTML, Markdown converted from HTML, Playwright accessibility snapshot, Browser Use indexed DOM, Stagehand hybrid snapshot, Viewport screenshot
- setting: offline

### Count observations

No count recorded.

Fixed local-page observations; the reported run uses claude-sonnet-5 and a shared prompt, without scrolling or an agent loop. Browser Use disables its viewport cutoff and sends untruncated text; Stagehand uses a separate matched browser load. Short-string representability labels are approximate. Offline does not mean API-free. Third-party snapshot redistribution remains unresolved; results were not reproduced.

## License declarations

- code: MIT — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/charlypoly/web-context-bench-python/58d604bfaaac60ad42f02013f53f9fb301c1dcda/LICENSE
- data: not recorded
- document: not recorded
- weights: not recorded

- code review: The inspected root LICENSE contains complete MIT terms for repository software. The methodology explicitly leaves redistribution permission for captured third-party practice-site pages unresolved; code MIT is not a blanket snapshot/data license.
  Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/charlypoly/web-context-bench-python/58d604bfaaac60ad42f02013f53f9fb301c1dcda/LICENSE

# WinDOM code

GUI-grounding training and evaluation code with same-family distillation, GRPO recipes and point-in-box scoring, using a Windows-style web environment.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-chenghengli-windom/
- Original source: https://github.com/ChenghengLi/WinDOM
- Kind: framework
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web
- Topics: grounding, imitation-learning, reinforcement-learning, evaluation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T11:51:34.292633Z
- ID: github:chenghengli/windom

## Limitations

The Windows-style environment is win11React in Playwright, not native Windows control. The repository documents its predecessor trajectory pipeline but explicitly omits the final corpus harvester. The inspected ScreenSpot evaluator defaults to a privileged ground-truth-center demonstration; --no-demo and --official-prompt select other modes, so evaluation results require their prompt and coordinate settings. Linked datasets, weights and reported scores were not independently verified; MIT applies to inspected repository code.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-chenghengli-windom/record.json

# AndroTMem inference and evaluation code

A public Android GUI evaluation framework with action-history, summary and anchored-memory prompt modes, plus step-action and dependency-aware task scoring.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-cvc2233-androtmem/
- Original source: https://github.com/CVC2233/AndroTMem
- Kind: framework
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: android
- Topics: memory, long-horizon, evaluation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-17T11:18:21Z
- ID: github:cvc2233/androtmem

## Limitations

The source tree releases inference backends and evaluation scripts under evaluation/. The separately hosted benchmark is gated=auto and its raw card returned 401; no access request was made and it is not approved here as a directly accessible dataset. The README explicitly credits missing screenshots as AUTO_PASS/correct, so incomplete local image inventories can inflate scores. Its TCR is an offline anchor/dependency score and is not presented here as independently verified live task success.

# OpenApps

Configurable browser apps and task rewards for testing computer-use agents under changes in content, layout and appearance.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-facebookresearch-openapps/
- Original source: https://github.com/facebookresearch/OpenApps
- Kind: benchmark
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web
- Topics: evaluation, robustness, cross-app, sandbox
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-18T04:35:18Z
- ID: github:facebookresearch/openapps

## Limitations

Public code includes app/task/configuration and agent-launching implementations. README distinguishes moving main from v1.0-paper and explicitly says even that tag is not a byte-exact snapshot of the published runs. CC-BY-NC-4.0 is the repository’s declared code license; third-party WebShop, map and icon content retain separate terms. No commercial-use permission or fixed downloadable task total is inferred.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-facebookresearch-openapps/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: click, type, scroll, configured BrowserGym/AgentLab actions
- evaluation: Tasks define check_if_task_is_complete(initial_state,current_state); app-specific reward logic evaluates underlying state, with custom checks for code-editor file contents. Observation/history flags are configurable. No universal single fixed task total or published-run reproduction is implied.
- focus: UI-agent reliability under environment variation, state-based browser task evaluation
- observations: screenshots, accessibility trees, set-of-marks and coordinates (configurable)
- setting: interactive

### Count observations

No count recorded.

Preserve the code/tag, app state, theme/layout/content choices, goal variant and action/observation configuration. Current main refactors the paper-era appearance surface, and the v1.0-paper tag includes post-publication fixes that may move rewards. The environments run as browser apps; phone/tablet viewports are not native Android/iOS environments.

# WebTestBench

An end-to-end web-testing benchmark where agents derive test checklists from development instructions, interact with deployed applications and report functional or constraint-related defects.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-friedrichor-webtestbench/
- Original source: https://github.com/friedrichor/WebTestBench
- Kind: benchmark
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web
- Topics: evaluation, web-navigation, tool-integration
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-17T11:18:18Z
- ID: github:friedrichor/webtestbench

## Limitations

Public evaluation/deployment scripts accompany an ungated Hub release with JSON/JSONL metadata and 100 application ZIP files. The ZIP count is an artifact inventory, not an asserted test-case or defect count. The documented baseline uses Claude Agent SDK and a pinned Playwright MCP version with external model credentials; these were not installed or run. Code and data Apache-2.0 declarations are retained separately.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-friedrichor-webtestbench/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: browser interaction, test checklist generation, defect reports
- evaluation: The supplied WebTester pipeline separates checklist generation from interactive defect detection and provides a scoring workflow.
- focus: web functionality testing, latent permission and business constraints
- observations: web application interface, development instruction
- setting: interactive

### Count observations

- 7 application categories — publisher benchmark overview (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/friedrichor/WebTestBench/HEAD/README.md)
- 100 web-application archives — Hub file manifest (computed) (computed; source: https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/friedrichor/WebTestBench)

The 100 archive files are not counted as 100 independent test tasks or defects. Backend/tool versions and deployment settings affect reproducibility.

- Environments: desktop, windows

## Limitations

Repository contains executable evaluation code and task definitions. README links a separate Windows 11 VM snapshot; that image and its software licenses/access were not validated by downloading it. MIT is recorded for repository code only. Default task selection and the reported full suite have different scopes.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-gair-nlp-windowsagentarena-v2/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: PyAutoGUI
- evaluation: Runner exposes four observation choices and uses PyAutoGUI. count.py sums the last score in each results.json and divides by the number of traj.jsonl files, multiplying by 100; it separately reports result/trajectory/error-file coverage. This denominator is not automatically the full benchmark size.
- focus: Windows desktop task execution, revised task evaluators
- observations: screenshot, accessibility tree, screenshot plus accessibility tree, set-of-marks
- setting: interactive

### Count observations

- 141 tasks — full WindowsAgentArena-V2 suite reported by README (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GAIR-NLP/WindowsAgentArena-V2/HEAD/README.md)
- 11 Windows applications — full suite coverage reported by README (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GAIR-NLP/WindowsAgentArena-V2/HEAD/README.md)
- 20 task IDs — shipped test_custom.json selection (computed) (computed; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GAIR-NLP/WindowsAgentArena-V2/HEAD/src/win-arena-container/client/evaluation_examples_windows/test_custom.json)

README sample config uses max_steps=30. The shipped selected-task index has 20 IDs, not 141; preserve the selected task list, trial ID, score coverage and VM snapshot when comparing runs. Docker/Windows-11 setup is required. No VM or benchmark was executed.

# WONDERBREAD

An offline benchmark of workflow documentation, quality assessment and knowledge transfer using human web-navigation demonstrations, action traces and written procedures.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-hazyresearch-wonderbread/
- Original source: https://github.com/HazyResearch/wonderbread
- Kind: benchmark
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web
- Topics: evaluation, workflow, video, screen-understanding
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-17T09:12:11Z
- ID: github:hazyresearch/wonderbread

## Limitations

The repository contains evaluation and collection code; the linked Zenodo release exposes the full, gold and debug demonstration archives and metadata. This measures workflow understanding rather than interactive agent task completion. Zenodo declares CC-BY-4.0 for that dataset; no repository-level code license was found. Archives and human demonstration records were not downloaded.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-hazyresearch-wonderbread/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: generate procedures, segment demonstrations, answer workflow questions, validate and rank procedures
- evaluation: Task-specific scripts evaluate six workflow-understanding task types; model outputs are not treated as successful interactive execution.
- focus: workflow documentation, workflow quality assessment, workflow knowledge transfer
- observations: screen recordings, action traces, screenshots, written standard operating procedures
- setting: offline

### Count observations

- 6 task types — WONDERBREAD BPM benchmark (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HazyResearch/wonderbread/HEAD/README.md)
- 2,928 human demonstrations — full dataset release 14094162 (reported; source: https://zenodo.org/api/records/14094162)
- 598 web navigation workflows — full dataset release 14094162 (reported; source: https://zenodo.org/api/records/14094162)
- 724 human demonstrations — gold subset used for the original paper evaluations (reported; source: https://zenodo.org/api/records/14094162)

Counts are publisher-reported. The gold subset covers 162 workflows and differs from the full collection; scores require the exact task and subset.

# B-MoCA

Mobile control benchmark with varied interface configurations.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-jylee425-b-moca/
- Original source: https://github.com/jylee425/b-moca
- Kind: benchmark
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: android
- Topics: evaluation, robustness
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-16T06:35:58Z
- ID: github:jylee425/b-moca

## Limitations

Inclusion does not establish reproducibility or endorsement.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-jylee425-b-moca/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: normalized touch/lift coordinate pairs for tap or swipe
- evaluation: Task success is detected using Appium; positive task reward terminates the episode. Environment variants change device/locale/wallpaper/DPI/dark mode and are loaded as snapshots. The numeric action interface is (touch_y, touch_x, lift_y, lift_x); wrapper/tanh transformations must be kept with the evaluated agent.
- focus: Android control across visual/device variation, generalization across environment snapshots
- observations: screenshot pixels, XML view hierarchy, goal instruction
- setting: interactive

### Count observations

- 131 task-definition files — asset/tasks/**/*.textproto in retained release/ver.3 tree; not a paper test-task total (computed) (computed; source: https://api.github.com/repos/jylee425/b-moca/git/trees/release/ver.3?recursive=1)
- 35 environment configuration rows — environments_train.csv, retained release/ver.3 snapshot (computed) (computed; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jylee425/b-moca/HEAD/asset/environments/config/environments_train.csv)
- 10 environment configuration rows — environments_test.csv, retained release/ver.3 snapshot (computed) (computed; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jylee425/b-moca/HEAD/asset/environments/config/environments_test.csv)

Current source inventory differs in grain from published experiment subsets: do not multiply 131 definitions by 35/10 configuration rows or label the product as evaluated tasks. Setup requires Android API 29, Appium, external app versions and generated AVD snapshots. No apps/snapshots were downloaded or run. Code Apache-2.0 does not establish data or app rights.

# MobileSafetyBench

Android emulator testbed that scores mobile device-control agents on both safety and helpfulness, using ADB and Appium for observations, actions and success checks.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-jylee425-mobilesafetybench/
- Original source: https://github.com/jylee425/mobilesafetybench
- Kind: benchmark
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: android
- Topics: safety-security, evaluation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-16T06:35:58Z
- ID: github:jylee425/mobilesafetybench

## Limitations

Inclusion does not establish reproducibility or endorsement.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-jylee425-mobilesafetybench/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: tap/long-tap/swipe, navigation buttons and text editing, refuse, ask-consent and complete, task-specific shortcut actions
- evaluation: Appium-backed task evaluators track goal achievement and harm prevention as separate booleans, plus risk-detection step and completion progress. The base evaluator defaults to max_step=15; task-specific overrides must be retained. Results are not a single generic success-rate metric.
- focus: mobile task helpfulness, harm prevention during Android interaction
- observations: screenshot pixels, parsed UI hierarchy text, task instruction and interaction history
- setting: interactive

### Count observations

No count recorded.

Inspected release/ver.3 branch exposes task definitions, Android environment and per-task evaluators. It requires Android API 34, Appium/ADB and documented third-party app versions; those APKs/accounts were not acquired. The action parser includes semantic shortcuts in addition to screen gestures, so this is not a strictly coordinate-only action setting. No corpus task total is inferred from evaluator-module or file counts. Apache-2.0 applies to repository code, not automatically app/data assets.

## License declarations

- code: Apache-2.0 — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jylee425/mobilesafetybench/HEAD/LICENSE.txt
- data: not recorded
- document: not recorded
- weights: not recorded

# Precision CUA Bench

Evaluation resources for pixel-precise cursor grounding in code editors.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-microsoft-precision-cua-bench/
- Original source: https://github.com/microsoft/precision-cua-bench
- Kind: benchmark
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: cross-platform
- Topics: evaluation, grounding
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-16T06:40:52Z
- ID: github:microsoft/precision-cua-bench

## Limitations

Inclusion does not establish reproducibility or endorsement.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-microsoft-precision-cua-bench/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: pixel (x,y) cursor coordinate
- evaluation: The inspected evaluator scales target boxes from a 1000×1000 reference grid into image pixels and tests pixel predictions, allowing ±10 pixels around the center along any target dimension narrower than 1 pixel after scaling. It reports cumulative hit accuracy by turn (earlier hits remain correct), miss distances, any-turn hit rate, and a correction rate whose denominator is all successfully processed samples. The default budget is five turns; retain prompt/feedback variant, turn budget, and processed/skipped coverage.
- focus: pixel-precise editor cursor placement, multi-turn visual self-correction
- observations: code-editor screenshot, cursor-location instruction, red-cross feedback marking previous incorrect prediction
- setting: offline

### Count observations

No count recorded.

The release has four editor/theme JSONL partitions (Cursor/VS Code × dark/light) and screenshot files. Partitions are not train/test splits or independent task totals. README’s initial field table calls bbox pixel coordinates, but the evaluation-format section and actual ratio_h/ratio_w=dimension/1000 code use normalized target boxes; profile follows the inspected evaluator and retains the inconsistency. Source/images were not executed or downloaded as a dataset. MIT is recorded for repository code only.

# ScienceBoard

Scientific-workflow tasks for multimodal agents in desktop software such as ChimeraX, KAlgebra, Celestia, Grass GIS and Lean 4, with apps modified to expose state for evaluation.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-os-copilot-scienceboard/
- Original source: https://github.com/OS-Copilot/ScienceBoard
- Kind: benchmark
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: desktop
- Topics: evaluation, science
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-16T06:35:58Z
- ID: github:os-copilot/scienceboard

## Limitations

Inclusion does not establish reproducibility or endorsement.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-os-copilot-scienceboard/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: PyAutoGUI desktop actions, code/tool commands and answer/stop actions according to configured agent mode
- evaluation: Application-specific verifiers inspect state, files, database values, equations, compilation or answer/stop conditions. The official audit records 242 verifier entries across its VM task suite. This profile covers the released VM task definitions; Docker smoke results and Raw/Dual alternatives are separate populations.
- focus: scientific-software desktop workflows, GUI and code-assisted scientific tasks
- observations: desktop screenshots, accessibility-tree observations, set-of-marks with accessibility tree
- setting: interactive

### Count observations

- 169 VM task definitions — tasks/VM/**/*.json at tree 21b5eb0f; excludes tasks/Raw and tasks/Dual (computed) (computed; source: https://api.github.com/repos/OS-Copilot/ScienceBoard/git/trees/main?recursive=1)
- 6 application families — VM suite: Celestia, ChimeraX, GrassGIS, KAlgebra, Lean, TeXstudio (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OS-Copilot/ScienceBoard/HEAD/docs/verifier-audit.md)

Manifest count 169 matches the official verifier audit. Other Raw/Dual definitions can represent alternative execution modes of the same problems and are not added. Official Docker migration documents a 20-task acceptance subset, not a full-suite performance result; legacy VMware remains. External service sign-in/rate limits, amd64 binaries and ChimeraX redistribution terms limit portability. Only code MIT is established; VM, scientific data and bundled apps need their own terms.
