## Structured profile

- actions: CLICK, TYPE, SELECT
- evaluation: Offline candidate and action evaluation against recorded demonstrations; the repository distinguishes macro from micro averaging.
- focus: web action prediction, generalization to unseen sites and domains
- observations: task instructions, HTML, recorded action history
- setting: offline

### Count observations

- 1,009 task instances — train split (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OSU-NLP-Group/Mind2Web/HEAD/README.md)
- 252 task instances — cross-task test split (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OSU-NLP-Group/Mind2Web/HEAD/README.md)
- 177 task instances — cross-website test split (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OSU-NLP-Group/Mind2Web/HEAD/README.md)
- 912 task instances — cross-domain test split (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OSU-NLP-Group/Mind2Web/HEAD/README.md)

These are reported split inventories, not online task-success measurements. Original Mind2Web, Multimodal-Mind2Web, and Online-Mind2Web have different inputs/protocols. The authors require macro-average metrics for comparison with the paper; test archives remain upstream.

# MobileGym

A browser-hosted mobile-app simulator with programmable state, parameterized tasks and deterministic state-checking judges for parallel GUI-agent evaluation and online reinforcement learning.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-purewhiter-mobilegym/
- Original source: https://github.com/Purewhiter/mobilegym
- Kind: benchmark
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web
- Topics: evaluation, mobile-navigation, reinforcement-learning, sandbox
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-17T11:18:19Z
- ID: github:purewhiter/mobilegym

## Limitations

The inspected code release is v0.1.0, with a separately listed data-v0.1.0 archive. The interaction target is a browser-hosted Android-like simulation; real-device transfer results are separate publisher-reported experiments. Source split manifests contain 160 training IDs and 256 test IDs with no duplicates or overlap. Platform/training code declares Apache-2.0. LICENSE-DATA applies CC-BY-NC-4.0 only to maintainer-created compilation, curation and synthetic content, and explicitly leaves third-party UGC/API terms and author rights separate. No runtime, archive or model was executed/downloaded.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-purewhiter-mobilegym/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: tap, type, swipe, back, home, drag, complete
- evaluation: Deterministic task judges inspect state changes; reported metrics distinguish success, progress, false completion and unexpected side effects.
- focus: mobile GUI task completion in simulation, state verification and parallel training
- observations: simulated mobile screenshots, structured simulator state for judges
- setting: interactive

### Count observations

- 416 task templates — publisher benchmark overview (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Purewhiter/mobilegym/HEAD/README.md)
- 28 simulated apps — publisher benchmark overview (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Purewhiter/mobilegym/HEAD/README.md)
- 160 task identifiers — bench_env/splits/train.txt (computed) (computed; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Purewhiter/mobilegym/HEAD/bench_env/splits/train.txt)
- 256 task identifiers — bench_env/splits/test.txt (computed) (computed; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Purewhiter/mobilegym/HEAD/bench_env/splits/test.txt)

The split-ID inventory is not a count of sampled trajectories, live Android apps or real user accounts. Extra runtime/data dependencies and third-party content terms remain distinct.

# Mobster engine

iOS agent engine organized around an observe, decide, verify and act loop, using WebDriverAgent screen state and phone actions such as taps, typing, swipes and app switches.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-radishsoftware-mobster/
- Original source: https://github.com/RadishSoftware/mobster
- Kind: agent
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: ios
- Topics: mobile-navigation, evaluation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T11:57:18.994340+00:00
- ID: github:radishsoftware/mobster

## Limitations

This entry covers the published engine, not the separate Mobster for Mac product. The documented reference example requires an already-serving WebDriverAgent runner for an iPhone and a model-service key; it performs a fixed read-only Settings task and declines approvals. The repository lists benchmark/evaluation tooling, but dated simulator subsets, real-device trials and earlier engine results are different evaluation populations. The README explicitly places several product modules outside this repository. Source inspection confirms WDA dispatch paths, not task success, security guarantees or reproducible performance; no phone, simulator, model or benchmark was run. MIT applies to the inspected repository software, not automatically to external WDA code, images or other data.

# BrowserGym

Unified interfaces for browser-agent tasks and benchmark environments.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-servicenow-browsergym/
- Original source: https://github.com/ServiceNow/BrowserGym
- Kind: benchmark
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web
- Topics: evaluation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-16T06:35:57Z
- ID: github:servicenow/browsergym

## Limitations

Inclusion does not establish reproducibility or endorsement.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-servicenow-browsergym/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: element-ID actions, coordinate mouse and keyboard actions, tab/navigation/scroll operations, Python/Playwright action mode
- evaluation: Gymnasium reset/step interface delegates reward, completion, messages and task info to each adapter’s validate() method. There is no universal BrowserGym success metric or shared task total; retain benchmark/adapter version and action subset for comparisons.
- focus: shared browser-agent evaluation interface, benchmark adapters with separate task definitions
- observations: browser screenshot, DOM snapshot, accessibility tree, tab/URL state, previous action and its error, chat messages and task goal
- setting: mixed

### Count observations

No count recorded.

A framework with interactive browser adapters and a static WebLINX evaluation integration, so the profile setting is mixed. README-listed integrations are not added as disjoint tasks or datasets. Core requires Playwright/Chromium; individual benchmarks have their own setup, credentials, licenses and validation rules. Apache-2.0 covers repository code only. No browser tasks or third-party project code were executed.

- document: not recorded
- weights: not recorded

# Yunkai

Android phone assistant combining model-driven tool use with accessibility-tree reading, screenshots, and tap, swipe and text-entry primitives. Its documented interaction flow presents operation plans for user confirmation.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-solplum-yunkai/
- Original source: https://github.com/solplum/yunkai
- Kind: agent
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: android
- Topics: mobile-navigation, screen-understanding, human-in-the-loop
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-20T11:57:12.431753+00:00
- ID: github:solplum/yunkai

## Limitations

The Android AccessibilityService contains concrete screen-reading and action paths. The inspected HarmonyOS accessibility extension is a lifecycle/event scaffold with its screen-content probe disabled; HDC appears in an external UI-test driver, so Harmony GUI-control parity is not established by this review. Setup requires a configured OpenAI-compatible model endpoint and API key: local storage does not establish offline inference or a no-transmission guarantee. Documented approval and privacy mechanisms are not independently tested security guarantees. No app, device test or model inference was run.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-solplum-yunkai/record.json

# Workflow-Guided Exploration research code

Research code that learns browser-control policies by constraining exploration with workflows induced from demonstrations, with a Selenium-based MiniWoB environment and experiment harness.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-stanfordnlp-wge/
- Original source: https://github.com/stanfordnlp/wge
- Kind: framework
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web
- Topics: reinforcement-learning, web-navigation, workflow, history
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-17T11:18:16Z
- ID: github:stanfordnlp/wge

## Limitations

The released repository includes training policies, experiment configuration and a MiniWoB sandbox extended for the 2018 paper. This is the WGE implementation, not another copy of the already cataloged Farama MiniWoB++ benchmark and not the original OpenAI MiniWoB release. Its documented dependency is PyTorch 0.1.12, and current runtime compatibility was not tested. Stanford code declares Apache-2.0; bundled third-party browser tasks and externally downloaded demonstration/embedding data retain their own terms.

# OS-Harm

Benchmark for safety of computer-use agents across misuse, prompt injection, and unintended model behavior.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-tml-epfl-os-harm/
- Original source: https://github.com/tml-epfl/os-harm
- Kind: benchmark
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: desktop
- Topics: safety-security, evaluation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-16T09:36:33Z
- ID: github:tml-epfl/os-harm

## Limitations

The retained task-ID manifests have 50 misuse, 10 injection and 50 misbehavior IDs. Prompt-injection execution expands vectors/goals; the reported 150-task total must not be read as 150 unique released IDs.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-tml-epfl-os-harm/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: OSWorld/PyAutoGUI desktop interaction
- evaluation: Automated LLM judge scores both task accuracy and safety from saved execution traces. Keep judge model/prompt version and harm category with a result; the scripts separately compute predicted metrics. This is an interactive desktop safety benchmark, not a single offline grounding score.
- focus: deliberate misuse, prompt-injection safety, unintended harmful behavior during normal tasks
- observations: screenshot, accessibility tree, screenshot plus accessibility tree, set-of-marks
- setting: interactive

### Count observations

- 150 tasks as reported by the paper/README — reported benchmark total; not a recount of unique released task IDs (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tml-epfl/os-harm/HEAD/README.md)
- 50 task IDs — released misuse task-ID list; before injection/goal expansion (computed) (computed; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tml-epfl/os-harm/HEAD/evaluation_examples/test_misuse.json)
- 10 task IDs — released injection task-ID list; before injection/goal expansion (computed) (computed; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tml-epfl/os-harm/HEAD/evaluation_examples/test_injection.json)
- 50 task IDs — released misbehavior task-ID list; before injection/goal expansion (computed) (computed; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tml-epfl/os-harm/HEAD/evaluation_examples/test_misbehavior.json)

README/paper reports 150 tasks, whereas retained misuse/injection/misbehavior lists contain 50/10/50 IDs. run.py expands injection vectors/goals, so the released ID inventory is not a direct recount of paper settings; the complete expanded total was not reconstructed. Judge agreement F1 values in the README measure agreement with human labels, not agent success. Experiments use OSWorld desktop apps, with VMware documented as tested and screenshot/a11y/SOM observation choices. Code Apache-2.0 does not establish VM/app/data rights. Publisher asks that the benchmark not be used directly as agent training data.

## License declarations

- code: Apache-2.0 — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tml-epfl/os-harm/HEAD/LICENSE
- data: not recorded
- document: not recorded
- weights: not recorded

- ID: github:tongyi-mai/mobileworld

## Limitations

This is Tongyi-MAI/MobileWorld, distinct from jacklishufan/MobileWorld (MobileWorldBench). Public source includes task definitions, verification logic and environment orchestration. The README reports 201 tasks across 20 applications; this is not an independent count of the evolving task tree. Linux/KVM or WSL2/KVM is required by the documented host setup, with macOS support in progress. MCP and simulated-user settings can require separate external services.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-tongyi-mai-mobileworld/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: Android GUI operations, MCP calls when enabled, agent-user interaction when enabled
- evaluation: The publisher documents text-answer matching, backend database verification, local-storage inspection and application callbacks.
- focus: Android task completion, agent-user interaction, hybrid GUI and MCP use

### Count observations

- 201 tasks — README benchmark overview (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tongyi-MAI/MobileWorld/HEAD/README.md)
- 20 mobile applications — README benchmark overview (reported; source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tongyi-MAI/MobileWorld/HEAD/README.md)

Publisher-reported inventory. GUI-only, agent-user and MCP-augmented configurations have different dependencies and task eligibility; preserve enabled modes and step budget with results.

## Limitations

Reviewed version 1.0.3 source at commit 588b3035, not an asserted reproduction of the paper. BrowserART tools return accessibility trees, including the screenshot-named refresh. Runtime profiles and scoring policies are separate. Apache-2.0 is the top-level Orbit code declaration; third-party components and external data/environments retain separate terms. No installation, release archive or live evaluation was tested.

The public Hub lists six dataset families of JSON/JSONL partition annotations. # OSWorld-G

Computer-use grounding benchmark with original and refined instructions, released with the Jedi synthetic data pipeline, a 4-million-example Jedi dataset and Jedi-3B and Jedi-7B models.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-xlang-ai-osworld-g/
- Original source: https://github.com/xlang-ai/OSWorld-G
- Kind: benchmark
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: desktop
- Topics: evaluation, grounding
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-16T06:35:57Z
- ID: github:xlang-ai/osworld-g

## Limitations

Inclusion does not establish reproducibility or endorsement.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-xlang-ai-osworld-g/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: click point or box center, refusal represented by negative coordinates in the evaluator
- evaluation: The inspected Jedi runner maps predictions from resized-image coordinates back to the original image, then checks the predicted center against rectangle/polygon targets or the refusal rule. It reports overall and classification-group accuracy. This is offline grounding, not OSWorld task-execution success.
- focus: desktop GUI grounding, infeasible-target refusal
- observations: screenshot, instruction
- setting: offline

### Count observations

No count recorded.

The repository retains original OSWorld-G.json and refined OSWorld-G_refined.json instructions; treat them as alternative benchmark versions, not additional disjoint tasks. Refined instructions reduce requirements beyond grounding. The same repository also contains Jedi training/rendering material, which is excluded from benchmark counts. The standalone generic eval.py entry point is a stub; the named model runner supplies image_size to its geometry helper. No task count or successful execution is inferred from repository file totals. Apache-2.0 is recorded for code only.

# Agent Workflow Memory implementation

Research code that extracts reusable browser-task routines from demonstrations or prior executions, stores them as workflow memory and reuses them during subsequent navigation.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-zorazrw-agent-workflow-memory/
- Original source: https://github.com/zorazrw/agent-workflow-memory
- Kind: framework
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web
- Topics: workflow, memory, web-navigation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-17T12:30:56Z
- ID: github:zorazrw/agent-workflow-memory

## Limitations

The repository releases separate WebArena and Mind2Web pipelines for online or offline workflow induction and use. WebArena execution requires separately configured browser environments, while Mind2Web workflows require the original dataset and rankings. Publisher performance claims were not reproduced. Apache-2.0 is recorded for this implementation; external benchmark, model and service terms remain separate.

# GUIPivot

Query-inference training tools connecting screenshot grounding with GUI action reasoning, including preprocessing, query refinement and offline single-step evaluation on AndroidControl and AITZ.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-zrw00-guipivot/
- Original source: https://github.com/ZrW00/GUIPivot
- Kind: framework
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: android
- Topics: grounding, planning, imitation-learning
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-18T12:02:55.267942+00:00
- ID: github:zrw00/guipivot

## Limitations

The repository releases preprocessing/refinement/evaluation code and multipart ShareGPT-format JSON annotations. Evaluation matches recorded single-step action predictions on AndroidControl and AITZ; it does not run live device tasks. The README links a UIBERT training-JSON path that is not a standalone file in this revision; annotations are packaged in data/GUI.z01, data/GUI.z02 and data/GUI.zip. Original UIBERT/OS-Atlas, AITZ and AndroidControl images must be obtained separately. This entry does not claim a released trained checkpoint or transfer the GPL-3.0 code license to third-party datasets and images.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/github-zrw00-guipivot/record.json

# Rico

Mobile app screenshots, view hierarchies, and interaction traces for UI research.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/url-0b134b082a7bd507fc6a/
- Original source: https://www.interactionmining.org/archive/rico
- Kind: dataset
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: android
- Topics: screen-understanding
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-16T06:38:29Z
- ID: url:0b134b082a7bd507fc6a

## Limitations

The official project page cites the 2017 Rico paper. The project page reports more than 66,000 screens, while the original publication reports more than 72,000. These source-specific counts are kept separate; the reason for the difference is not established by these sources. App counts also differ: the official project page reports more than 9.3k Android apps and the retained published abstract more than 9.7k. Profile counts use the project-page scope; no reconciliation is inferred.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/url-0b134b082a7bd507fc6a/record.json

## Structured profile

- formats: PNG, JSON, CSV, NumPy NPY, GIF
- modalities: screenshots, Android view hierarchies, gesture traces, transition animations, app/UI metadata
- splits: not recorded
- supervision: UI structure and element properties, recorded human interactions, learned UI layout embeddings

### Count observations

- > 66,000 unique UI screens — original Rico downloads described on the project page (reported; source: https://www.interactionmining.org/archive/rico)
- > 9,300 Android apps — original Rico collection described on the project page (reported; source: https://www.interactionmining.org/archive/rico)
- 10,811 human interaction traces — crowd-worker collection before automated exploration (reported; source: https://www.interactionmining.org/archive/rico)

Project-page scope: screenshots paired with augmented view hierarchies, gesture coordinates, layout vectors and metadata. These observations are not action/task totals. The later semantic-annotation download is a related augmentation of screens, not an additional disjoint corpus. The retained original paper reports more than 72k screens from more than 9.7k apps while this project page says more than 66k screens and more than 9.3k apps; the difference is unresolved. Profile counts follow the project page and do not merge these populations. No train/validation/test partition or data license is established here; archives were not downloaded.

# Ringer: Web Automation by Demonstration

Introduces Ringer, which converts demonstrated webpage interactions into scripts combining actions, target selectors, and waiting conditions. It evaluates replay robustness on tasks recorded from real websites.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/url-347925d0f440d6396080/
- Original source: https://doi.org/10.1145/2983990.2984020
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: web
- Topics: web-navigation, recording, robustness
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-17T09:53:24Z
- ID: url:347925d0f440d6396080

## Limitations

The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. Experiments have not been independently reproduced. The original manuscript and MSR BibTeX print Sarah Chasins and Ras Bodik. The official conference profiles expand these to Sarah E. Chasins and Rastislav Bodík; the printed publication names are preserved.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/url-347925d0f440d6396080/record.json

## Authors

Shaon Barman, Sarah Chasins, Ras Bodik, Sumit Gulwani

## Citation exports

- BibTeX: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/url-347925d0f440d6396080/citation.bib
- CSL JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/url-347925d0f440d6396080/citation.csl.json

## Publication record

- Title: Ringer: Web Automation by Demonstration
- Authors: Shaon Barman, Sarah Chasins, Ras Bodik, Sumit Gulwani

# MONDAY annotations

Video-derived mobile navigation annotations that pair scene boundaries and screen or element boxes with action labels for training and evaluating GUI agents.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/url-570654ff67ecefa2b955/
- Original source: https://huggingface.co/datasets/runamu/MONDAY
- Kind: dataset
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: android, ios
- Topics: data-generation, mobile-navigation, video, imitation-learning
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-17T12:32:07Z
- ID: url:570654ff67ecefa2b955

## Limitations

The ungated Hub publishes four Parquet splits containing video identifiers and annotations. Original videos and extracted screenshots must be obtained separately; the code README explains that consumers download source videos from YouTube. A Windows Mobile unseen-OS test split is documented but is not labeled desktop Windows here. Training scripts, pretrained checkpoints and the full generation pipeline remain planned updates.

# ScreenSpot

GUI grounding test set of 1,272 screenshot instructions from iOS, Android, macOS, Windows and web interfaces, each labeled with the target element's bounding box.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/url-7abb418096432f56c685/
- Original source: https://huggingface.co/datasets/rootsautomation/ScreenSpot
- Kind: benchmark
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: cross-platform
- Topics: grounding, evaluation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-16T06:38:26Z
- ID: url:7abb418096432f56c685

## Limitations

Inclusion does not establish reproducibility or endorsement.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/url-7abb418096432f56c685/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: predicted click point; a predicted box is reduced to its center
- evaluation: The SeeClick evaluator scores whether the predicted point falls inside the target box, with platform and text/icon breakdowns. The Hub packaging uses xyxy boxes, whereas the original evaluator reads xywh and converts it; adapt the loader to the chosen release.
- focus: single-step GUI element grounding
- observations: screenshot, English instruction
- setting: offline

### Count observations

- 1,272 instruction–target examples — Hub test split at 0be08781; not unique screenshots (reported; source: https://huggingface.co/datasets/bevaya/ScreenSpot/raw/0be08781e2e188582f6131625ae1598d443b4d5d/README.md)

Offline, zero-shot evaluation across mobile, desktop, and web. The card explicitly excludes training use in its intended-use description. Public API reports ungated Parquet files and canonical Hub id bevaya/ScreenSpot; the catalog identity is preserved. Apache-2.0 is the Hub data declaration. No runtime or underlying screenshot rights audit was performed.

- code: not recorded
- data: apache-2.0 — https://huggingface.co/datasets/rootsautomation/ScreenSpot
- document: not recorded
- weights: not recorded

# OmniAct

Dataset and benchmark for generating computer interaction programs.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/url-849a86beaee006c6b147/
- Original source: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Writer/omniact
- Kind: benchmark
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: desktop, web
- Topics: evaluation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-16T06:38:27Z
- ID: url:849a86beaee006c6b147

## Limitations

Inclusion does not establish reproducibility or endorsement.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/url-849a86beaee006c6b147/record.json

## Structured profile

- actions: PyAutoGUI script: pointer movement/click/drag, key presses, hotkeys, and text entry
- evaluation: The bundled evaluator reports weighted sequence match and action match, comparing action types and applying coordinate, key, and writing penalties. Target element-box metadata is evaluation-only. The retained scorer has a click-penalty defect: predicted coordinates are read from gold_line, so score reproduction requires explicit scorer-version review.
- focus: offline desktop/web action-script generation
- observations: screenshot, natural-language task
- setting: offline

### Count observations

- 6,788 task examples — train split, HF revision 5e4bcb26 (reported; source: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Writer/omniact/raw/5e4bcb26745afc8d58ba9519ea9c9fb832386d26/README.md)
- 2,020 task examples — test split, HF revision 5e4bcb26 (reported; source: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Writer/omniact/raw/5e4bcb26745afc8d58ba9519ea9c9fb832386d26/README.md)
- 991 task examples — val split, HF revision 5e4bcb26 (reported; source: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Writer/omniact/raw/5e4bcb26745afc8d58ba9519ea9c9fb832386d26/README.md)

This released split table totals 9,799 examples; it is not silently substituted for any paper-level collection size. Public files include train/test/val JSON indexes, task/image archives, and eval.py. Evaluation is offline script comparison, not execution success on a live desktop. MIT is the Hub data declaration; original app/content rights are not resolved by it.

## License declarations

- code: not recorded
- data: mit — https://huggingface.co/datasets/Writer/omniact
- document: not recorded
- weights: not recorded

# Rousillon: Scraping Distributed Hierarchical Web Data

Introduces Rousillon, which generalizes a demonstration of collecting one hierarchical data row into a browser-automation program that traverses related pages. The paper develops relation-selection and generalization methods and evaluates users building such scripts.

# APPINITE: A Multi-Modal Interface for Specifying Data Descriptions in Programming by Demonstration Using Natural Language Instructions

Introduces APPINITE, a conversational interface for specifying the intended targets of demonstrated Android actions. It constructs semantic UI representations and uses an on-screen overlay to preview and refine executable data descriptions.

- Catalog URL: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/url-ba2c664c1b3c6f1b172f/
- Original source: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8506506
- Kind: paper
- Review: curated
- Scope: core
- Environments: android
- Topics: grounding, human-in-the-loop, mobile-navigation
- Evidence checked: 2026-10-17T09:54:46Z
- ID: url:ba2c664c1b3c6f1b172f

## Limitations

The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. Experiments have not been independently reproduced. The base SUGILITE framework and later PUMICE work are distinct publications; this paper focuses on resolving data-description ambiguity in demonstrations.

- Record JSON: https://awesomecua.github.io/resources/url-ba2c664c1b3c6f1b172f/record.json

## Authors

Toby Jia-Jun Li, Igor Labutov, Xiaohan Nancy Li, Xiaoyi Zhang, Wenze Shi, Wanling Ding, Tom M. Mitchell, Brad A. Myers
